found: Measured: after the reboot the agent replayed the afternoon's jobs from the oldest (102 started, 40 ok, 62 failed - mostly guards refusing), fifty at a time after a reconnect, on shared clones; it had inferred 'pending' from a missing result. Before that it stalled at 22:29 CET with nothing logged until the reboot. No alert could reach the author - every channel went through the agent. Harm: none - four replayed pull requests, all the legitimate tad 0.4.0 pin bump; no direct pushes, tags, releases or phone actions; tools and clones restored. The root: a job is a script with no record of its life. Proven answers: durable execution's event history and heartbeats (Temporal), leases with fencing tokens (Kleppmann; Patterns of Distributed Systems), a dead man's switch watched from elsewhere (Healthchecks), crash-only recovery (Candea and Fox), run-once jobs with deadlines (Kubernetes), idempotency keys (Stripe), a working tree per job (git worktree). Replayed 2026-11-12: the old agent's real log of 2026-11-11, read line by line through oco-agent's rules (oco-agent/replay): of the 357 jobs the old agent started over six runs, oco-agent would have started 255 and refused exactly 102, each because it had already finished - the first at 23:16:24, the moment the replay began. The journal it kept (764 rows of tad data) checks out and answers SQL. 2026-11-12, from the whole system's log: the machine did not sleep and its network stayed up through the stall; a USB device was disconnected at 22:25:28 with nothing after it going wrong, so the phone looks innocent. The stall was inside lab-agent's daemon. Its GitHub client is built with no limit on how long a request may take (src/github.rs: ureq::AgentBuilder::new().build()), so one connection that hangs holds the polling loop for ever - which fits every fact, though nobody watched it hang. oco-agent's client limits every request to 20 s. The desktop is set to suspend after an hour without input, and lab-agent keeps it awake only while a job runs. 2026-11-12, proven: the replays come from lab-agent's reading of what is done. already_handled lists its results folder through GitHub's contents API, which returns at most 1,000 entries and says nothing of the rest: the folder held 1,135; the first replayed job of the second replay (1794436981-after-reconnect) had its result, but was not among the 1,000 listed. Every job past the thousandth looked unfinished. Both replays - 102 jobs on 2026-11-11 and 25 after the boot on 2026-11-12 - share this one cause. The 2026-11-12 replay changed no repository (no commits since the boot) but put tad 0.4.0 back on the lab (restored to 0.5.0). 2026-11-12, later - the stall is proven too, and it has the same cause as the replays. lab-agent sees new jobs through the same contents listing of its jobs folder, cut silently at 1,000 entries. The folder holds a placeholder, .keep, which sorts before every job; when lab-agent started its last job before the stall (22:29:23), the folder held 999 jobs - with .keep, exactly 1,000. Every job submitted after that lay past the end of the listing: the agent was alive, polling, and blind. The earlier note here that a request with no time limit was the probable cause was wrong as the main cause; time limits are added anyway, since a hang should never be silent either. One cause - a listing that stops without a word - made the stall, the replay of 102 jobs, and the replay of 25 after the boot.

found: The world has tried it under several names - specialised workers under a supervisor, hierarchical teams, blackboard systems, stateful agents - and converges on one split: the expert is a role and a body of written knowledge; a session is a disposable worker that takes the role up. Gas Town says it outright (an agent is a persistent identity, sessions are cattle; any session can hand off and restart from its hook). Anthropic's long-running harness found compaction alone not enough and had every fresh session get up to speed from a progress file, git and a feature list; its context-engineering guide names notes outside the window as the tool for iterative work with milestones. Claude Code itself moved this way: subagents may keep a per-role MEMORY.md, and agent teams start each teammate from project context and a spawn prompt, never the lead's history, and do not restore teammates on resume. Against expertise held in a long context: models recall worse as input grows (Chroma, context rot; Anthropic's attention budget), repeated summarising erodes detail (ACE: context collapse, brevity bias), and a session of 1000-1800 messages re-reads all of it each turn - after an idle hour without the cache, at full price - so a standing expert answering an occasional question is the costliest and not the most reliable way to answer it. Against a central router: a supervisor that relays every message plays telephone - lower scores and more tokens than agents handing off directly (LangChain); misalignment between agents (lost context, withheld information) is one of the three failure groups in 1600 traces (MAST). What works (Cognition, 2026): one writer per thing, other agents adding intelligence not actions; a consult works best given a fork of the asker's full context. Blackboard systems route by a shared record agents read, not by a relay. For us: most of the audio expertise is already rows in docs (5 research, 2 decisions, 27 backlog items name the microphone); what is not written is the tacit part - dead ends, where the experiment patches are, what hung the phone - and it now lives in hand-over notes outside any repository.
question: Should linux-phone-oco keep standing expert sessions, one per hard domain (audio, modem, sleep...), with the orchestrator routing questions to them - or keep expertise somewhere else?

found: Everyone who shares such a resource gives it one owner that serves a queue. Hardware test farms: LAVA has a single scheduler that assigns devices to submitted jobs (Mesa reaches its boards only through it); CI-tron puts one gateway in charge of its devices under test, and postmarketOS runs its phones behind one. Gas Town gives the merge queue to one role, the Refinery, which merges every change to main one at a time; the role outlives any session - a new session for it takes up the next step, nudged by patrols. The actor model and the single-writer principle say the same for state: one owner, reached only by messages it takes one at a time. Anthropic's research system parallelises only what is independent. Put with this commons' own finding that experts are written down, not standing (decision 2026-11-17-experts-written-not-standing): the keeper is a lasting role whose sessions are disposable - each works until its piece lands or its context grows large, writes its hand-over into the resource's how-it-stands record and ends; others prepare in parallel and queue items with their proofs; a named query over the backlog is the queue; a schedule or patrol wakes the role when the queue has work and no keeper is live; and the resource's own tool still holds the lock for every change, so the keeper adds flow, not safety. Raised by the author on 2026-11-17 for the lab's phone.
question: How should many agent sessions share one resource that only one may change at a time - a test device, a lab machine, a release or merge queue - so that work flows without races and without a session kept alive forever?

found: Acoustically, through the paths a person uses, with the analysis in Rust: during the call the uplink capture that the call needs anyway (1 channel on TX_CODEC_DMA_TX_3, the bottom mic) is written to a file instead of thrown away. The phone plays a pattern of three short tones (e.g. 800, 1300, 1900 Hz, 200 ms each, 300 ms apart - inside the 300-3400 Hz every voice codec keeps) on the loudspeaker at the manifest's quiet level; the bottom mic hears it at once (proves the injection) and sends it up the call; the echo comes back down and plays on the earpiece, and the same mic hears it again 150-1500 ms later (the network's round trip; acoustic reflections are under 20 ms). A Goertzel envelope per frequency finds the pattern twice; the echo counts when the same order of tones recurs at one delay, 15 dB above the noise, and the delay is reported. Before the echo call, a call to the tone line (99702) proves the downlink alone, so a missing echo says uplink (or the line) rather than everything. Cost: one call of at most 25 s (dial, about 8 s to answer, 5 s of pattern, hang up; a hard timeout), at most once a day, a landline-rate number: inside a flat, or under 10 ct per day on prepaid. Skips cleanly, as unknown: no modem, no SIM, not registered, no voice interface, no call path (call-audio-path failing), the daily call already made, or the number unset in the manifest. A pass proves works for modem-calls. If q6voice exposes in-call record/playback ports (downstream's VOICE_RECORD_RX, incall music), a digital loop could replace the acoustic one later; unknown on this driver.

found: What is: devlab-health, a static Rust runner (lab-tools/health), runs shell checks on the phone after every boot in two layers (base, shell): 11 generic in lab-tools and 5 of surya's own in surya-lab; each prints 'pass|fail|skip TEST COMPONENT detail' and docs' tests table says what each pass proves. The phone has no Rust toolchain (it has python3, which the lab refuses), so rust-script (stable, 0.36 on the lab) cannot run there and would need a toolchain and network on the phone; Cargo's own single-file scripts (frontmatter, cargo PR 16569) are still nightly-only in Cargo 1.99. Shape that fits: shell stays for what is a reading (sysfs, a command's output; ten readable lines), and anything with numbers, timing or a state machine (tones, echoes, calls, sleep counters) is a subcommand of one static multi-call Rust binary shipped with devlab-health (e.g. devlab-health tone find, devlab-health call echo), built with its unit tests and recorded fixtures on the lab and cross-built by health/build.sh; rust-script is the lab's prototyping and one-off analysis tool against recordings fetched from the phone, a prototype becoming a subcommand once it is kept. Coverage is read off the data: a query of every device's components with no test that proves works, and a layer per cost - base, shell, then telephony (calls and data, gated by budget and once a day) and witnessed (needs a person).

found: They agree. (1) One small entry that is always read and routes onward, saying what each target is for: llms.txt, the root AGENTS.md (nearest wins), PhotoCraft's Read/Why orientation table, Johnny.Decimal's index, datapackage.json. (2) What is always loaded is kept small: CLAUDE.md under 200 lines, no more than ten per level, llms.txt's skippable Optional. (3) Detail in stages: Skills' name and line, then body, then linked files; Claude Code loads nested CLAUDE.md only when its subtree is touched; context engineering keeps lightweight identifiers - paths, stored queries - and loads content just in time. (4) Small units with stable addresses: evergreen notes whose titles work like APIs, numbered ADRs, Wikidata's Q and P ids. (5) Facts apart from explanation: Diátaxis' reference against explanation, Wikidata statements and infoboxes beside prose. (6) One decision per record, superseded rather than deleted (Nygard, MADR). (7) Every statement is about an item by its id and cites who says so (Wikidata). (8) Views are generated from the source data (PhotoCraft's scorecard, Mintlify's llms.txt). Tensions: hierarchy against association (fixed buckets vs dense links - a small fixed index with free links beneath answers both); one file against many (concatenation does not save context; loading on demand does). No source measured how much any of it speeds an agent - the measure here is docs' own (kb-navigation-measured).

found: The decimator-to-DSP leg worked all along: each silent recording began with ~0.5 s of ringing (-1774 settling to exact 0), the high-pass filter draining a constant input - the decimator ran and its output reached TX_CODEC_DMA_TX_3, but no samples entered it. The cause was upstream of the decimator: the capture link named the TX SoundWire controller's DAI 0, its playback DAI (qcom_swrm_register_dais makes the first num_dout_ports DAIs playback, and this controller has one dout port), so sdw_stream_add_master was never called and the codec's ports never programmed. The same one-dout-port shift moves master port numbers by one (ports start at 2; swr2's qcom,ports-* arrays begin with 0xff). For DMICs the same reading held: with no clock on the pin the data line is static and the filter removes it. So: start-up ringing then exact zeros means no input reaches the decimator - look at the source (SoundWire stream, DMIC clock), not the DMA or the AFE port. The AFE port is the vendor's too: TX AIF1 on TX_CDC_DMA_TX_3 (45111 = 0xB037), accepted by this ADSP.
question: What made the TX decimator to codec DMA path deliver zeros, and what does a capture of zeros tell?

found: Two built-in analog microphones on the WCD9375: the bottom one on AMIC1 (mic bias 1) into ADC1, the top one on AMIC3 (mic bias 3) into ADC2 with its input mux at INP3; the headset mic is AMIC2 (bias 2) on the same ADC2 at INP2. ADC1 comes back over the TX SoundWire bus on master port 2, ADC2 needs its own master port 3 (qcom,tx-port-mapping <2 3 4 5>): sharing port 2 with ADC1 lost the top mic and turned the bottom one to full-scale noise (pulpoff). No digital mics: pulpoff names LPI gpio7-11 NC, among them gpio8-11, the DMIC clock and data pins (vendor gpio26-29), and records both mics through ADC1/ADC2 on mainline. The TX DMIC1-3 routes read on 2026-11-17 come from sdmmagpie-qrd-overlay.dts, Qualcomm's QRD reference board kept in Xiaomi's tree, which declares the SWR_ADC0/ADC2 routes beside them. Measured on the phone (bring-up, 2026-11-17 04:37 UTC, test/surya-mic with <&swr2 1>): mic-records pass and mic-hears-speaker pass, a 1 kHz tone at -19.4 dBFS against -76.3 dBFS of noise through ADC1. found: Through s2idle and CPU idle, not suspend to RAM: the firmware offers no PSCI system suspend, so with userspace frozen the CPUs enter their idle states, the last one down takes the cluster power domain to its deepest state (PSCI OS-initiated mode, hierarchical CPU idle), and as the cluster powers off the application processor's RPMh sleep votes are flushed to the always-on subsystem (rpmh-rsc attached to the cluster domain). The always-on subsystem then lowers CX and DDR when no processor votes for them: CX collapse (cxsd), then AOSS sleep (aosd), the floor. The SoC counts each in its own memory (rpmh-stats, read through qcom_stats), so reaching the floor is measured, not inferred. Without OS-initiated mode the cluster domain would stay always on and the votes would never flush; surya's firmware has it.
question: How does a Qualcomm phone reach its lowest power state on mainline?

found: The modem's messages (QMI over QRTR on glink) are handled even in s2idle (IRQF_NO_SUSPEND), but userspace is frozen, so nothing rings. found: The codec dropped off both SoundWire buses because ASoC puts every idle component into its sleep pin state, and the codec's sleep state drove its active-low reset low (traced: snd_soc_bind_card committed it 0.24 ms before both interfaces went UNATTACHED). Without a sleep state the codec stays attached and capture prepares (linux-phone-oco/linux PR #4); the SoundWire pin-mux fix is PR #3. Capture still yields exact zeros: the built-in microphones are digital mics (vendor: TX DMIC1-3 on LPI gpio26-29, function 1, mic bias 1 and 3); this ADSP rejects the VA capture port, so they go through the TX macro to TX_CODEC_DMA_TX_3; with the VA DMIC clocks forced on the TX path still reads zeros, as it does from ADC1 - the next fault sits in the TX decimator to DSP leg. found: In stages, never at once. A first translator is written outside - in another language, as an interpreter, for a subset, or by hand - and needs only to be enough to carry the language's own saying of itself; that saying is then run through it, and then through itself, and the two results are compared: where they differ, one of them is wrong. So the outside is not thrown away when the inside can first speak; it stays beside it until the inside says the same, and what remains outside afterwards is small and is what touches the machine. For ocoeco this gives the order: move what is already declared (what an entry asks, how a row is named, where it is kept) before what acts on a surface (reading the words, writing the row); run the lens beside the program's saying and compare before taking the program's away - which is what was done for entering, tried as a place's own lens first; and keep the kernel that stays in the program small and named - the engine that answers queries, reading from surfaces, writing rows. What the comparison is for a compiler, a look kept before and compared after is here.

found: Others who read a surface as a table agree on three things. The shape of a table is data: declared, not coded. The kinds of surface are few, and each is a small adapter in the program that makes rows when asked - nothing is stored. And which surface a table reads from is said beside its shape, the where a parameter. So here: a table's shape is said once - by the lens that defines it, else by the place's own declaration, else read off its rows; where its rows come from is a route, said in the language; and a table is entered as itself where no entry has its name. Three open things - a route said by a lens, a shape said where entries do not read, a next step that is words - were one question: what a table is, and where its rows come from.

found: Looked at ourselves first (2026-11-13). Of 36 parts in the lenses built in: 14 only filter the rows of one kind; 15 count or gather; 9 bring two kinds together; 8 take a name apart to find what it points at; 1 is placed. All 22 tables are declared as a minimum - a row may carry more - and all are keyed by id alone: they are kinds of thing with an id, not tables in the strict sense. And the work about what bears on what is done outside any table: 280 lines of the program check links, 473 rewrite them when rows move, 59 walk a chain. So tables serve us for counting and gathering, for a whole thing readable on one line, and for checks when written; they do not give identity, edges, walking, what points at a thing, or what was. In the world: a table is one way of sorting facts, not the facts - Datomic keeps facts and answers row-like and column-like questions from the same ones; identity can be what a thing is, with names as labels (Unison); a graph can be declared over tables that exist and walked in the engine we use (SQL/PGQ); and text at rest with a graph when asked is a working arrangement (Logseq), whose newer form warns against giving up the text. In power a table does nothing a graph of facts cannot; in practice it gives a mature, fast engine and a row a person can read whole. The middle man is at the asking, not at rest: at rest we already keep things with ids and links - nodes and edges, written as text.

Keeps: decisions with why, rejected, research, sources. Lacks: the relation between decisions - one refining or replacing another is written as text today, three times on 2026-11-12. WORK - best: visible flow, pull, limits, ageing (Kanban, Reinertsen). Keeps: the backlog's flow, driver, next, since, waits_on; oco-agent's journal says what actually ran. Lacks: why this work - its link to the milestone or decision it serves. RESULTS - best: evidence that can be checked, not a claim. Keeps: glimpses, workings with evidence, gathered releases, activity and test runs. Lacks: evidence as a link to the thing that proves it. LOOKING BACK - best: the After Action Review, hansei. Keeps: reflections. Lacks: nothing essential. PROBLEMS - best: the andon - a problem visible the moment it happens, to everyone, until it is dealt with. Keeps: nothing of its own; attention is computed for the flow only. Lacks: the lens itself - 21 release runs failed unseen and a watcher was silent for a night on 2026-11-12. The largest gap. INVITATION - best: a need marked where it is, small and well-defined, fillable by whoever passes (Wikipedia's citation needed, good-first-issue labels, citizen science, device owners filling a support table). Keeps: nothing. Lacks: the entity - what is needed, of what kind (information, a test on a device, feedback), where, and how to give it. What open commons add to Toyota's room. THE SKY ITSELF - what makes lenses one dome: relations seen as connections, the story, and time. Keeps: about 860 links that resolve, the essence a star tells, and history in git. Lacks: the relations declared - the dome's continuity rests on them. So, in order: declare the relations (among them one decision refining another, and work serving a milestone); the problems lens; the invitation; how a finding is known and evidence that links; then lenses as data.

found: The best of it is Toyota's obeya, the big room: begun on the Prius project because no single person held the knowledge the work needed, its walls showed purpose, plan, progress, problems and countermeasures together, so that anyone entering saw the whole and problems became visible. found: Two things share the name monad and neither is the passthrough lens. In Haskell a monad chains steps that each carry something extra; what composes lenses there is plainer - optics compose as functions, and the identity is the lens that passes everything. Leibniz's monad is a standpoint: a simple substance mirroring the whole from its point of view - nearest to a place one looks from. What the world found as the smallest whole set: the identity; three ways into a shape - one part of what is side by side (a lens), one case of what is one of several (a prism), each of many (a traversal); two ways to go together - one after another, and side by side; and two directions - get and put - held to a law, that what is put is what is then got. Shapes themselves are made of the same two: this and that, this or that - down to the bit, the smallest this-or-that. A region of bits (from, how many) is the simplest lens there is, and formats are declared so. Against ocoeco (2026-11-14): both ways of going together exist (a shape read across lenses; places). The identity does not: a table is kept as another kind of thing than a lens, though it is the passthrough of what a place keeps. A lens's two faces, glimpse and focus, are put and get, but their law is nowhere said - one sign of it shows by accident: a table nothing brings into focus. And a lens is still a bundle of four things - what data is, how it enters, what bears on what, what comes into focus - with how it is laid out mixed in. Parts that count or gather only read: through those nothing can be put, and that is as it should be.
question: Is there a sense in a monad in our ecosystem - can all lenses be expressed from a simplest, passthrough lens - and how does it fit with shapes coming down to bits?

found: The author, 2026-11-12: a lens propagates light, it lets it through; by itself it shows nothing - it is not a screen or a picture - and the word showing falls off the full picture, as if from another domain. In optics a lens is defined by this: it transmits light and brings it to a focus; a telescope's lens gathers a star's faint light and focuses it, so that a blur becomes something one can make out. So the second face of a lens is its focus, and the act is to focus. It is plain and can be guessed (focus the lens on a star); it says the true thing about the data - nothing is made, the same data is brought into focus; and it leaves the showing where it happens, on the fulldome. The whole then reads as one picture: a star gives off light, its data; a glimpse catches it where it is fresh; a lens lets it through and brings it into focus; the fulldome is where it is seen; to observe is to gather the light of many stars. Shine is no act of ocoeco: it is what a star does by working.
question: What does a lens do with what passes through it - what is its second face called?
